fields.title: Polka: the second region requested by the board
fields.summary: After a competitor's outage, the board asks for a second region. The answer is due in two weeks.
fields.decisionPrompt: What is your answer to the board? State the price of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. Following a public incident where a competitor was down for 6 hours, the board of directors requests a plan for deploying a second region. The response deadline is two weeks.
fields.brief/objective: Answer the board in a way that directs money toward the class of failures we actually experience.
fields.brief/constraints: Two weeks to respond. A multi-region setup takes a quarter of work and 400 thousand per month.
fields.brief/task: Decide what to tell the board and back it up with numbers.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Buy protection against what actually happens to you
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A loud failure at a neighbor shifts the conversation toward the most expensive solution, and it often doesn't even address the root cause. The test is simple: break down someone else's incident by mechanics and look at your own outage history. If none of your incidents were infrastructure failures, a second region buys peace of mind rather than reliability—while costing a quarter of work and ongoing money.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Three availability zones in a single region. Over the past six months, 4 incidents totaling 85 minutes, none of which were related to infrastructure failure—all were software-related or caused by external providers.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Active-passive multi-region: a quarter of work, 400k/month. Active-active: two quarters, 600k/month plus ongoing friction in making changes.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: An hour of downtime during peak time costs about 100k in non-recoverable losses. Over six months, damage from all incidents combined was about 70k.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: The cause was an erroneous configuration rolled out to all environments simultaneously. They have two regions.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Deploy an active-passive second region. One quarter, 400k/month.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: answers the request literally. Protects against a class of events we have never experienced. Does not protect against what happened to the competitor—a faulty configuration rolls out everywhere. Costs a quarter of the roadmap.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Refuse, justify with calculations, propose an alternative
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Refuse, justify with calculations, propose an alternative. Two weeks for preparation and discussion.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: honest and well-reasoned. Proposes investing the same resources into things that reduce actual damage: gradual rollout, reducing detection time, drills. Risk that the stance will be perceived as reluctance to solve the problem.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Analyze the competitor's incident and fix its exact class
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Three weeks. Gradual configuration rollout, traffic splitting tests, automatic rollback.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: addresses precisely what scared the board. Cheap relative to a quarter of work. Does not provide a second region, which will require explanation.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Start with preparation: extract state, remove zone bindings, make infrastructure reproducible
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Start with preparation: extract state, remove zone bindings, make infrastructure reproducible. One and a half months.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: makes a second region possible in weeks when it is needed, instead of a quarter. Improves the system regardless of the decision. Does not provide a region right now.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Fails to calculate ROI on reliability investments
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not understand what geography protects against
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not check whether the measure matches the threat
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Multi-region setup is not mapped to the class of failures it prevents
